name: Hallohesh
overview: Hallohesh was a male official responsible for half the district of Jerusalem, demonstrating a position of local authority and administrative responsibility. His role is noted specifically in the context of Jerusalem's governance. No tribal affiliation or additional personal notes are recorded for him.
namesAndTitles: The name Hallohesh means "the whisperer." This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God, but it carries a distinctive Hebrew meaning that may reflect a characteristic or reputation associated with him.
familyAndRelationships: Hallohesh is identified as the father of Shallum, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, Scripture does not record any additional family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Hallohesh's significance lies in his administrative role within Jerusalem during a time of rebuilding and restoration, as indicated by his official capacity over half the district. His mention alongside his son Shallum underscores a familial link contributing to the community's leadership. His presence in the biblical record highlights the importance of local governance in the post-exilic period.
